sources.name: World Bank Open Data API (World Development Indicators)
sources.what_it_gives: Historical GDP per capita, inflation, unemployment, and net migration by country, annual, via free REST JSON API.
sources.api_pattern: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/{ISO3}/indicator/{CODE}?format=json&date=YYYY:YYYY&per_page=1000 ; indicators: NY.GDP.PCAP.CD (GDP/capita), FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (inflation %), SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS (unemployment %), SM.POP.NETM (net migration)
sources.historical_range: 1960-2025 (varies by indicator/country)
sources.license_note: CC BY-4.0, free, no API key required

sources.name: BIS Residential Property Price Statistics
sources.what_it_gives: Long quarterly nominal and real residential property price index history for ~60 countries.
sources.api_pattern: https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_SPP/1.0/{FREQ}.{REF_AREA}?format=csv ; FREQ=Q, REF_AREA=2-letter country code (AU, US, DE, CA, GB...); omit REF_AREA entirely to pull all countries

sources.license_note: Free, BIS open statistics, cite BIS
sources.notes: Human page https://www.bis.org/statistics/pp.htm 302-redirects to a JS-heavy dashboard (dataportal/pp.htm); the old flat-file guess full_pp_csv.zip is dead (404). Use the SDMX v2 REST API instead - confirmed working, returns both nominal and real index series (UNIT_MEASURE 628/771) back to 1970-Q1 through 2026-Q1 for Australia. Full API docs: https://stats.bis.org/api-doc/v2/.

sources.name: OECD Data Explorer SDMX API
sources.what_it_gives: House price indices (nominal & real, multiple measures) by country/quarter; same SDMX mechanism extends to rents, tax wedge, wages, and hours worked via other dataflow IDs.
sources.api_pattern: https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/{AGENCY},{DATAFLOW_ID},{VERSION}/{REF_AREA}.{FREQ}.{MEASURE}.{UNIT_MEASURE}?format=csv ; leave a segment blank to wildcard it (e.g. AUS.Q.. wildcards MEASURE+UNIT_MEASURE). Full dataflow catalog: https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/dataflow/all/all/latest?references=none
sources.historical_range: 1970-2026 Q1 (house prices, Australia; varies by country/dataset)
sources.license_note: Free, OECD open data
sources.notes: The task's sample URL was missing one dimension (SDMX error 'expecting 4 got 3'); this dataflow's correct dimension order is REF_AREA.FREQ.MEASURE.UNIT_MEASURE (4 dims), confirmed via the dataflow structure query. data-explorer.oecd.org itself is a JS SPA (not directly scrapable) but the underlying sdmx.oecd.org REST API works well and is the right integration point. Rents/wages/tax-wedge/hours-worked live under different dataflow IDs not individually re-verified this session - discover via the catalog search URL above (~1500 dataflows total).

The official REST API at api.bls.gov IS reachable and returns a well-formed JSON envelope (verified: status REQUEST_SUCCEEDED for a syntactically valid but non-existent test series ID, i.e. the endpoint mechanism works). Exact metro-level Software Developer series IDs were not independently nailed down this session - the coding agent will need to construct them from BLS's published OEWS series-ID formula. v2 API without a free registration key is capped at 25 queries/day (500/day with one).

sources.name: Eurostat ICT Specialists in Employment (isoc_sks_itspt)
sources.what_it_gives: Country-level count (thousand persons) AND percentage-of-total-employment of ICT/tech specialists, annual - the CS/IT-specific employment series requested.
sources.api_pattern: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/{dataset_code}?format=JSON&lang=en ; append &geo=XX&time=YYYY to filter. Dataset isoc_sks_itspt dimensions are freq/unit/geo/time; unit=THS_PER (headcount, thousand persons) or PC_EMP (percentage of total employment).
sources.historical_range: 2004-2025 annual (22 years), 37 areas (EU27_2020 aggregate + individual EU/EFTA/candidate countries)
sources.license_note: Free, Eurostat open data, cite Eurostat
sources.notes: Task's exact sample URL worked as-is (HTTP 200, real data, 30KB) - no variant needed. Confirmed via dimension inspection that the 'unit' dimension includes BOTH THS_PER (Thousand persons, actual headcount) and PC_EMP (Percentage of total employment), so this single dataset gives both the raw CS/IT employment COUNT and the share metric, per country per year. This directly satisfies the CS/IT-specific employment requirement at country level with 22 years of history.

sources.name: Eurostat Total Employment - National Accounts (nama_10_pe)
sources.what_it_gives: Country-level total employment headcount (thousand persons, national-accounts concept), annual, long history - pairs with the ICT-specialist series above to compute CS/IT share of total jobs.
sources.api_pattern: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/{dataset_code}?format=JSON&lang=en ; nama_10_pe dimensions are freq/unit/na_item/geo/time - filter na_item=EMP_NC (Total employment, national concept) or EMP_DC (domestic concept), unit=THS_PER. Task-suggested alternates une_rt_a (unemployment RATE, annual) and lfsi_emp_a (employment/activity RATES not counts) also confirmed live.
sources.historical_range: 1975-2025 annual (51 years), 44 countries
sources.license_note: Free, Eurostat open data, cite Eurostat
sources.notes: Task suggested une_rt_a or lfsi_emp_a as the total-employment dataset; both return HTTP 200 valid JSON, but neither is a clean raw headcount: une_rt_a is an unemployment RATE, and lfsi_emp_a's unit dimension is THS_PER+PC_POP i.e. mixes a real headcount with a %-of-population rate (2003-2025, 38 geos). nama_10_pe is the better match - it has an explicit na_item='Total employment national concept' (EMP_NC) in Thousand persons, covering 44 countries back to 1975 (7 na_item categories total, incl. EMP_DC domestic concept, SAL_NC/SAL_DC employees, SELF_NC/SELF_DC self-employed - useful sub-breakdowns). All three endpoints verified live (200, real JSON) this session; nama_10_pe recommended as the primary 'total employment' series.

sources.name: Indeed Hiring Lab Job Postings Index (GitHub)

'Software Development' in the US and IT-related sectors elsewhere), and for several countries by state/metro/city - a job-POSTINGS demand proxy for CS/IT and total jobs, country and city level, with history.

Files vary per country: aggregate_job_postings_{CC}.csv (country total/new postings), job_postings_by_sector_{CC}.csv (incl. Software Development sector for US), metro_job_postings_us.csv + state_job_postings_us.csv (US only), city_postings_gb.csv + regional_gb.csv (UK), provincial_postings_ca.csv (Canada). Directory listing via https://api.github.com/repos/hiring-lab/job_postings_tracker/contents/{CC}
sources.historical_range: 2020-02-01 to present, daily (repo self-updates weekly; latest row observed 2026-07-24)
sources.level: city (US metros pop 500k+, UK cities); also country and state/province/region for all covered countries
sources.license_note: Free, open (LICENSE file present in repo); cite Indeed Hiring Lab

Confirmed live: US metro_job_postings_us.csv has 1,403,039 rows spanning 2020-02-01 to 2026-07-24 across US metro areas (by CBSA code); US job_postings_by_sector_US.csv (194,013 rows) confirms a 'Software Development' category with daily values across the same range. The UK's GB folder DOES include city_postings_gb.csv for city-level data. Ireland is explicitly excluded from sector-level data per the repo README.

sources.name: BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov - historical depth reality-check (supplement to bls_oes)
sources.what_it_gives: Confirms api.bls.gov CAN return genuine occupational EMPLOYMENT COUNTS (not just wages) at both national and metro level, but reveals the public/unregistered API's practical historical depth for OEWS series is very shallow for the series tested - the bls.gov website/flat-file mirror needed for true multi-year metro history remains fully blocked from this environment.
sources.api_pattern: POST https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/ with body {"seriesid":["OEUN000000000000015125201"],"startyear":"2020","endyear":"2025"} ; series ID = 'OE' + U (not seasonally adjusted) + area-type (N=national, M=metro, S=state) + 7-digit area code + 6-digit industry code (000000=all industries) + 6-digit SOC occupation code + 2-digit datatype code (01=employment).
sources.historical_range: Empirically only 2025 returned data for both the national and San Jose-metro 'Software Developers' (SOC 15-1252, datatype 01=employment) series tested; 2015-2024 all came back 'No Data Available' for the identical series IDs, and the pre-2018-SOC-revision codes (15-1132/15-1133, the old split 'Applications'/'Systems Software' categories) came back 'Series does not exist' entirely.
sources.license_note: Public domain (US government)
sources.notes: Re-confirmed the website block: https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm, https://download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/oe/, and 5 years of https://www.bls.gov/oes/special.requests/oesm{YY}ma.zip flat-file guesses (24, 23, 20, 15, 12) ALL returned HTTP 403 regardless of headers - a full site-wide block, not a missing-file issue. On the API side: series OEUN000000000000015125201 (national, all industries, Software Developers, employment) returned a real headcount of 1,687,890 for 2025; the metro equivalent for San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara CA (CBSA 41940, series OEUM004194000000015125201) returned 87,350 for 2025. Both are genuine employment COUNTS, confirming the API mechanism works as the existing bls_oes entry states - but neither series had ANY data for 2015-2024, so multi-year OEWS metro history is NOT reliably obtainable through the unregistered public API for this occupation. Pipeline implication: try a registered BLS API key (may unlock more years), or a non-blocked egress path to the bls.gov flat files / data.bls.gov, rather than relying on the public API alone for OEWS history.

sources.name: Teranet-National Bank House Price Index (Canada, city-level JSON)
sources.what_it_gives: Canadian city-level house price index, monthly - the direct city-level house-price-history match for Canada, via an undocumented but open JSON endpoint behind the public housepriceindex.ca charts.
sources.api_pattern: https://housepriceindex.ca/_data/indx_data.json returns {profiles: {cityCode: {name, latest indx_value, ...}}, data: {indx, sa_indx, spc, indx_ch, sa_indx_ch, spc_ch: {cityCode: [monthly values...]}, meta: {start_date, end_date}}}. https://housepriceindex.ca/_data/indx_data_releases.json is release-schedule metadata only, not data.
sources.historical_range: 1990-06-01 to 2026-06-01 (433 monthly points); individual cities start later than the array start - e.g. Vancouver has data for the full range from index 0, while Toronto/Calgary/the 11-city Composite only start around index 96-104 (roughly 1998-1999) - exact per-city start is the first non-null array entry
sources.level: city (33 Canadian metro areas + 2 composite series: 'Composite 11' and 'All Metropolitan Areas')
sources.license_note: No explicit open-data license found on-page - Teranet/National Bank branded proprietary index, page is publicly viewable but terms of programmatic reuse are unstated; verify before production/commercial use
sources.notes: Best surprise of the session. housepriceindex.ca required curl -k (its TLS chain didn't validate against curl's default CA bundle) - worth checking before production use. The homepage has NO visible CSV/download button; the real data source was found only by grepping the homepage's raw HTML for '.json' references, which surfaced /_data/indx_data.json - a 558KB undocumented file behind the interactive chart widget, with a 'profiles' object (metadata + latest value per city, 35 entries) and a 'data' object containing full per-city monthly arrays (index, seasonally-adjusted index, sales-price composite, plus *_ch change variants) and an exact {start_date, end_date} meta block. A fully free, structured, 36-year city-level dataset with no login/paywall, sitting undocumented behind a marketing site.

sources.name: Numbeo per-city historical cost-of-living page

sources.historical_range: content references years from roughly 2000 through 2026 on the Berlin test page
sources.license_note: Free to view on-site; Numbeo's bulk/API access is a separate paid product (see existing 'numbeo' entry)
sources.notes: QUICK CHECK ONLY, per task instructions. The task's exact guessed pattern https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/city_history.jsp?city=Berlin returns HTTP 404 (a 'General Error Message' page) - that .jsp/query-string form is retired.
